title: a scratch bus whose caller is gone serves on for hours
intention: A --scratch bus that no caller has reached for N seconds, holding no open connection, no ask in flight and no undelivered mail, ends itself with its cause recorded; the live house bus never does.
why: Measured 2026-11-19 on akiendelllinux: 31 scratch bus units served on after their callers were gone, one for 2h 7min on 1.3 s of CPU, until a hand stopped 29 of them. Their homes were never removed, so the existing home-gone exit could not fire. A process that outlives every caller is a leak the next mind has to find by hand.
traces_to: CP4 through the bus charter's lazy-init why (the next ask respawns a bus, so an idle one costs only its memory and its unit) and Law 7 (the exit records its cause in stops.jsonl).
how: Owner: the bus machine (cairn/devices/cairn/machines/bus). The starter remote._spawn (bus_client, remote.py:233) is unchanged. The bound sits in the bus because the bus alone knows whether anything is open or standing; the starter only knows it launched. _HomeWatch.service_actions already runs every poll and already ends a bus whose home is gone; the idle check sits beside it and leaves by the same door (stop.set, then shutdown on a thread), so a scratch home's spill and asks file are written exactly as at any other exit. N = CAIRN_BUS_IDLE_S, default 1800 s. N IS A HYPOTHESIS: bus.log records no ask or connection timing (measured), so the longest gap between asks a real long proof makes on its scratch bus could not be read. 1800 s is 3x the longest single held request measured (581.7 s, b0e65cf8a77e's queueme, 2026-11-12); that is a held connection, which keeps the bus busy anyway, not a gap. D2 writes idle_s_max into every stop record so the next reading of stops.jsonl sets N by measurement. THE TESTER-ID CASE KEEPS ITS COLLECTMODE STOP: CollectMode=inactive-or-failed only reaps the unit record once the process has exited, by any cause, and the tester's end-of-run stop is a SIGTERM that serve records as cause 'signal'. A proof's bus is reached continuously, so the tester's stop normally comes first. If the idle exit comes first, the tester's stop finds an inactive unit and is a no-op. Both go through the one stop path, so the two exits never fight.

clauses.claim: only a --scratch bus idles out: a serve(scratch=True) at a scratch home with CAIRN_BUS_IDLE_S short and nothing open exits after it with a stops.jsonl record of cause 'idle'; a serve(scratch=False) under the same short N is still serving well after it

nothing is lost across an idle exit: no idle exit while a connection is open, an ask is in flight, a row is undelivered, or a shim held by spec is wired, even past N. 'Subscribed' covers both kinds: a spec-held subscription lives only in the bus process's roster, so it is guarded (the bus does not exit while one is wired); a subscription on disk (cairn/devices/**/shim.py) is rebuilt by the respawned bus's roster. After an idle exit, a call through a RemoteBus handle opened before it respawns a bus at the same home, and a re-held fixture echo (never a real device's shim) is answered by the new pid

N is read, not guessed: with CAIRN_BUS_IDLE_S unset N is 1800 s, and every stop record (idle, signal, verb) carries idle_s_max, the longest gap in seconds between one connection closing and the next opening over that bus's life

decisions.text: D1: serve sets server.scratch = scratch beside server.home (server.py:1159). _Handler counts open connections on the server and stamps server.last_idle_at = time.monotonic() when the count falls to 0. _HomeWatch.service_actions, after the home-gone check: if getattr(self,'scratch',False) and open == 0 and nothing is in flight or undelivered (the same accessors take_over_asks/return_the_backlog read) and no shim held by spec is wired (process._by_spec whose device_id process._is_wired) and monotonic() - last_idle_at >= N, print 'bus: idle <s>s with nothing open or standing — exiting', stop.set('idle', {'idle_s': s, 'n_s': N}), and start the shutdown thread exactly as the home-gone branch does. N = float(os.environ.get('CAIRN_BUS_IDLE_S', '1800')).
D2: idle_s_max is kept on the server (the max of each gap closed, plus the open gap at stop) and _record_stop adds it to every stop record's detail-level fields as 'idle_s_max'.

D3: a red-first proof, one tooth per clause, PROVES {1,2,3}, harness copied from test_every_stop_records_its_cause.py: serve in a child process at a scratch HOME with CAIRN_BUS_IDLE_S=2, read <home>/stops.jsonl. Tooth 2 holds a connection open past N, then posts mail to a subscribed recipient across a respawn. Tooth 3 imports the default from server inside the tooth. Tooth 2 also holds the fixture echo (bus_proof_echo, by spec) and shows the bus stays up past N while it is wired; the respawn half re-holds the echo on the respawned bus and reads the new pid from its reply. Every unit the proof starts is stopped by name in its finally.

measured.saw: 31 cairn-bus-<hash> units ran `serve --home <h> --scratch` since 15:00 with no tester id; cc_0 found 29 standing and stopped them at 23:09:37 (bus.log: 'bus: stop ... cause signal sender_pid 1798'). Unit ffd7fdacc1: started 21:02:20, stopped 23:09:37, 1.269 s CPU over 2h 7min.
measured.how: journalctl --user over Started cairn-bus-*.service lines; systemctl --user show; bus.log stop lines

measured.saw: CORRECTION to the first reading ('every home missing'): all 31 homes are PRESENT (ls -ld; mtimes 23:09, the stop, not a removal). bus.log carries 0 'is gone — exiting' lines ever, though _HomeWatch.service_actions (server.py:822) ends a bus whose home is gone and server.home is set on every serve (1159). The units outlived their CALLERS, not their homes: a shell exported CAIRN_BUS_HOME=$(mktemp -d /tmp/xx.XXXX), ran cairn verbs (a cairn pre-commit's tester --reseal --stage reaches the bus via _announce_seals; any verb asking the bus does too), and never removed the dir.
measured.how: ls -ld per unit home from the journal's --home argument; grep -c over ~/.cairn/logs/bus.log; reading server.py

measured.saw: CORRECTION on whose: units c44a3a41b2 (/tmp/bsp.ALKX) and ffd7fdacc1 (/tmp/bsp.6gNj) were spawned at 21:02 from ~/dev/src/wt-splice/cairn by akienasus_cc_0's castsplice script, which exported a scratch CAIRN_BUS_HOME around cairn cast, outlinecheck and the commons commit. An earlier report that none were mine was wrong.
measured.how: bus.log 'client: bus spawn attempted as cairn-bus-<hash>' and 'bus: serving <home>/bus.sock ... root <cwd>' lines matched to the script's echoed BUS line

measured.saw: bus.log records no per-ask or per-connection time (its line kinds: backlog, spawn attempted, serving, stop, took over, tracebacks), so the longest gap between asks a real long proof makes on its scratch bus cannot be read from it.
measured.how: line-kind census of ~/.cairn/logs/bus.log (15602 lines) with digits and paths masked

measured.saw: a shim held by spec lives only in the bus process's roster; a respawned bus rebuilds its roster from shim.py on disk alone (roster.shim_for -> bus_client._device_shim_module -> rack.shim_of over _CLASS_ROOT; DeviceRoster takes no root override), so an idle exit would lose a spec-held wire
